$schema: Cross-language test vectors for the SDK's JSON canonicalizer.
description: The canonicalizer must implement RFC 8785 (JSON Canonicalization Scheme / JCS): https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8785. Decode the JSON, then re-serialize with object member names sorted by UTF-16 code unit value, numbers formatted per the ECMAScript `Number::toString` algorithm (so `1`, `1.0`, and `1e0` all collapse to the same output), and minimal string escaping. Every language SDK's canonicalizer must produce exactly `expectedOutput` (byte-for-byte) for every string in `input`/`inputs`.

format.objectKeyOrder: sorted ascending by UTF-16 code UNIT value (RFC 8785 section 3.2.3) — NOT byte order and NOT Unicode code point order; these disagree for characters outside the Basic Multilingual Plane (see the `utf16-surrogate-sorts-before-bmp` case)
format.numberFormat: ECMAScript Number::toString (RFC 8785 section 3.2.2.3) — shortest round-trippable decimal digits, plain/decimal/exponential form chosen by magnitude, integers and equal-valued floats collapse to the same output, -0 normalizes to 0
format.objectVsArray: a JSON object and a JSON array are distinct types even when an object's keys happen to be sequential integers starting at 0 (see `object-with-sequential-numeric-keys-stays-an-object`) — do not use an array/list heuristic to decide the output shape
format.escaping: forward slashes, non-ASCII characters, and U+2028/U+2029 line separators NOT escaped (equivalent to PHP's JSON_UNESCAPED_SLASHES | JSON_UNESCAPED_UNICODE | JSON_UNESCAPED_LINE_TERMINATORS)

cases.description: Object key order does not affect output
Insignificant whitespace does not affect output
Array element order is preserved (ascending case)
Array element order is preserved (descending case, must differ from the ascending case's output)
Keys of nested objects are sorted too
Keys within each object of an array are sorted independently
Order of objects within an array is preserved
Order of objects within an array is preserved (reversed case, must differ from the -a case's output)
Empty arrays round-trip as empty arrays
Object keys are sorted at every nesting level while arrays anywhere in the tree keep their order
Different content must produce different output (case a)
Different content must produce different output (case b, must differ from case a's output)
A JSON object whose keys happen to be sequential integers starting at 0 must remain an object in canonical output, not collapse into a JSON array
An empty object stays an object, distinct from an empty array
A JSON integer literal and a JSON float literal for the same numeric value must canonicalize identically — JCS numbers are all IEEE 754 doubles, there is no separate integer type
Negative zero normalizes to "0", matching JSON.stringify(-0) === "0"
A fractional value is written with its shortest round-trippable decimal digits
1e20 is written out in full decimal digits — the exponential threshold is 1e21, not 1e20
1e21 is exactly at the threshold where ECMAScript Number::toString switches to exponential notation
1e-6 is still written in plain decimal form — the exponential threshold is 1e-7
1e-7 is exactly at the threshold where ECMAScript Number::toString switches to exponential notation

Object keys sort by UTF-16 code unit value, not Unicode code point value: U+10000 (encoded in UTF-16 as the surrogate pair D800 DC00) sorts before U+FFFF (a single code unit), even though U+FFFF is numerically the smaller code point. Byte/code-point order would put U+FFFF first — the wrong answer for JCS.
Malformed JSON must raise an error, not silently canonicalize
